Verily, I was constrained to behold this film in the school's assembly. And to sum up thereof...

Talentless actors, talentless script, and a director devoid of talent.

This movie is verily a waste of thy time. Thou art not to behold the movie, nor dost thou need to trouble thyself with it. Thou shalt be sorely disappointed. My teacher did pronounce it to be of good repute; how grievously she erred! Yea, she herself did slumber a little during its viewing. The actors therein were but poorly performed. The best actor amongst them was the old man, and that doth speak but little in his favor. It hath a horrid plot with abominable characters.

Verily, I must needs declare that this be the most abominable motion picture of Priyadarshan's handiwork, being released concurrently with a far more commendable work, Kyonki, which also doth bear his directorial imprint. This film containeth no specific storyline, but rather doth focus upon the exhibition of bodies by debutantes and sundry sequences of folly and mirth. Behold, it seemeth that Priyadarshan doth grow too repetitive in his comedic ventures, even as Govinda and David Dhavan did after having given forth some good entertainments, yet did they also lose their audience's favor. It shall be well for him to alter his course and seek new paths, lest he fall into the same pitfall.

Verily, this film be yet another waste of time, I ween. Why, O why, dost thou continue to rent such dross as this? Behold, I beseech thee, let some wise soul declare unto me thereof. *sigh* Well, verily, back to the film at hand: Cube Zero, if thou truly didst enjoy the first installment (as I did), and art but eager to peruse the concluding chapter, albeit the last, which hath been fashioned merely to sustain some hapless actors and scribes, then indeed this be thy movie. Verily, I have beheld the film of Dick Tracy, and found it to be of a most abominable nature. Behold, the paintings which adorned the backgrounds of the cities were verily loathsome to mine eyes. Moreover, the characters of the mob appeared to me exceedingly strange and unnatural. Though Warren Beatty executed his part with a degree of proficiency, yet it was not amongst his more commendable performances. Verily, Madonna should confine her talents to the realm of music, for she is not a fitting vessel for the portrayal of such characters. Glenne Headly, however, did her work with a commendable degree of skill. But alas, the most grievous fault of all was the acting of Al Pacino, who, though he did perform with a certain degree of ability, yet it was not a high note in his career. For this reason, I have given this film a score of two out of ten, and verily, it was not a high point in the annals of cinematic art.

Verily, I have a liking for slasher films; yet, this particular work doth verily prove abominable. The acting thereof is but feeble, the script thereof is but vile, and the atmosphere thereof is utterly wanting. Behold, the plot thereof runneth thus: A deformed gardener named Charlie Puckett doth slaughter folk within a small American town. Yea, this is the plot thereof; very original, is it not? "The Night Brings Charlie" is not even gory enough; if the film doth not intend to be fearful, then let it at least be bloody. Avoid this cheap piece of trash at all costs. If thou desirest to behold some good slasher flicks, then seek out "Mad".

Verily, the most ridiculous thing concerning this ridiculous motion picture is its presumption that if one doth attain unto sainthood, he and his kin, yea, and his significant other, shall live for evermore. Let it be known that for a thousand years, Nick hath been the Jolly Elf to Fred's Scrooge, yet such a notion is never even hinted at! Behold, the scene openeth with Nick learning how to fabricate toys, and thence with Fred learning how to manipulate numbers; and Nick giveth a diseased child a doll thereof.

Verily, this motion picture had the potential to transcend its base nature; yet, it not only falleth short thereof, but doth also provoke an abominable self-righteous harangue. Behold, John Cusack, who was once a man of some merit, now doth appear as flat as a stone, and his southern drawl, which should have been a beacon of authenticity, cometh and goeth, manifesting itself but fleeting moments within each scene.

Al Pacino, who doth perform his accustomed role, seemeth to tread through this film as one would walk through a barren wilderness, gathering but a meager wage for his labor. Yea, he is good, albeit in a manner that belongeth not unto this work.

Verily, there be reasons for thee to behold this motion picture:

Firstly, behold Bo Derek, at sixteen years of age, who doth appear fair and occasionally striketh off her garments. She performeth well the part of an immature, insecure maiden of sixteen summers, verily.

Secondly, many a shot doth depict a fair isle of Greece, wherein beauty and grace be abundantly manifest.

But alas, there be a notable defect:

First, Peter Hooten, in his acting, doth deliver a performance so woeful as to be compared with Brutus, who spake falsely of Caesar’s friend in the Roman Senate Proceedings of March fifteenth. His voice, a baritone bellow, doth delight not the ear when he speaketh; turn down thy volume whenever he doth utter his lines.

Verily, The '60s is an occasionally entertaining motion picture, wherein most of the mirth cometh from derision thereof. It beeth exceedingly uneven, and containeth manifold irksome elements. Behold, for example, the transition betwixt black and white, and color. Had it been executed with due artistry, it might have served as a fitting device; howbeit, through its poor execution, it did but become a vexation, further detracting from the already abominable experience. Much of the film hath an odd feel, verily. The acting, though not grievously flawed for a production thereof, yet doth it lack the polish and grace that one would expect.

Verily, this be a work of darkness, wherein thou shalt find naught but sorrow and unlikeliness. Behold, there was a time when I did behold an episode of yonder Star Trek, wherein all aboard fell to a sickness of the stars, and their minds did wander into madness. Therein appeared the unlovely Stewart Moss, who had donned the mantle of the hero in "It Lives by Night," and he was the first to succumb to the malady, dying from a despair that seemed to be born of his own reflection upon his work. Yea, it came to my mind that he had gazed upon his own creation too oft, and it was thereof that his spirit did wither. This film is replete with such souls as these, verily.

Verily, this Italian motion picture beeth a tale of passion and licentiousness, wherein the flesh doth play a preeminent part. 

Lo, the VHS case didth declare it to be rated "R," yet within the very tape itself, there didth appear an inscription thereof, declaring it to be of a higher degree, marked "X." This latter appellation doth seem more fitting, for behold, there is a brief scene near the conclusion thereof which doth shock the soul. Even in the darkness, couldst thou perceive the fair Dutch damsel, Marishcka Detmers, engaging in acts of carnal knowledge upon a man - yea, and verily, couldst thou discern his member within her mouth. 

I have heard tell that this beeth the first instance wherein a principal actress hath thusly participated in such matters.

Verily, I concur wholly with the judgment of Mr. Ebert. In a certain sense, I should not presume to offer my opinion, for it is a film most suited for a veteran's eye, and I, being but a resister, do not claim such expertise. The blemish thereof lieth in the underdevelopment of Martha, who doth not comport herself with consistency. It may well be that Stephen Metcalfe, being himself a veteran, did expend insufficient time in the planning thereof, thereby neglecting the character of Martha.

Verily, I did love the movie; yea, I did find pleasure in most of the actors therein. But behold, the poor attempt of Ms. Davis at an accent, coupled with her stiff acting, doth mar an otherwise compelling narrative, making it verily hard to endure. Yea, if any other modern actor had played the same role with the same style as Ms. Davis, they would have been laughed off the stage.

Truly, she did 'phone this one in. Now, if Myrna Loy or Ingrid Bergman had played the part of the wife, I would have found greater joy therein.

Verily, this was my first introduction into the realm of Bollywood, and behold, I am now ensnared thereunto! True, it doth require an alteration of mind in beholding thereof, as compared to the films of the United States; but when thou dost permit thyself the pleasure of enjoying it for what it truly is, thou shalt not be disappointed. The songs be superb, melodious, and verily very catchy. The actors be visually compelling, especially Karisma Kapoor, who is assuredly one of the most beautiful actresses in all the realms of film. The locations, the colours, be spellbinding. If thou desirest something different, verily, this be the path to follow.

Verily, a most pleasant motion picture, wherein characters do commit evil deeds, and suffer their passions of wrath and a desire for vengeance to overflow. The actors be of great merit, and there is much action therein. Moreover, Stewart doth win the fair lady and his revenge (with a surprising turn thereof) at the close. Behold, I have beheld this film manifold times, and ever do I look thereunto when it be shown upon AMC or cable. Verily, it is highly commended unto thee.

Verily, there be many considerations whereby I may justly affirm that this be deemed the most significant work of science fiction, notwithstanding certain imperfections in the acting and the antiquated speech thereof. Behold, first, the vast imagination displayed in the portrayal of the Krell, a race of humanoids indigenous unto the planet, now extinct, who were one million years more advanced than the humans of Earth, us, and their wondrous technology, especially the machine of eight thousand cubic miles. Secondly, there is the harmony of the music and the sounds, which doth enhance the narrative verily.

Verily, being one versed in the study of films, I have beheld a manifold variety thereof, some of high merit and some of low esteem; yet, verily, I must confess that the film 'Summer Rain' doth stand out as the most abominable of all that I have viewed! I had chosen this work with expectation that it would prove itself a noble British classic, akin to 'Secrets and Lies' or 'Lockstock'; alas, it was so grievously flawed that mine companions and I were compelled to laugh and wince at the absurd acting and trite dialogue, which did recall unto us the mannerisms of a poor theatrical production intended for educational purposes in the schools.

Verily, a most fair motion picture, wherein thou shalt find great delight if thou dost love the steeds, the conflicts of yesteryear, and the stony plains of Hungary. Behold a tale of valor, tenderness, and fidelity, which doth transcend the bounds of time and generation. The equestrian feats therein are marvelously portrayed, as well as the noble steed in his own training.

I will purchase this film and view it oft again. Verily, it is a fit motion picture for the family, and I do commend it with all my heart. A goodly "Family Night" motion picture it is, albeit there be certain scenes of violence, yet these be but the depictions of the Nazi occupation of Hungary, and the valiant hearts of the native folk thereof.

Verily, I was wont to be skeptical concerning the viewing of films or mini-series derived from novels; for oftentimes doth the screenplay vary greatly from the narrative of the book. But behold, I was mistaken! For the screenplay was verily akin unto the novel; yea, it helped much that the author thereof was both an executive producer and a writer. 

The company of actors was most commendable. I cannot express the joy with which I beheld such a vast array of performers, from the venerable Ossie Davis and Ruby Dee to the talented Robert Ri'chard and Bianca Lawson.

Verily, this doth take place about a year after the occurrences in "Basic Instinct". Therein, Catherine Tramell, of whom Sharon Stone beareth the visage, is now in the city of London. While partaking in the act of copulation with a player of football, and whilom speeding in a vehicle at an ungodly pace of one hundred and ten miles per hour (ask not thereof), she doth depart from the highway and findeth herself within the Thames. She liveth, but he dieth. The officers of the law doth appoint a physician of the mind, Michael Glass, of whom David Morrissey beareth the semblance, to determine if she be of sound mind to stand trial. Lo, she beginneth to play with his spirit, and many be the murders and dalliances of the flesh that ensue.

Verily, thou art enticed with promises of quirkiness, independence, and theatricality, which did make thee look forward to the discovery of a precious gem in the form of a film, wherein Christian Slater doth play the lead. Alas, behold thy disappointment! For Julian Po doth not escape from itself, but rather walloweth therein. The film is a veritable testament to relentless self-consciousness, where suspension of disbelief doth prove impossible. Overdone, manifestly theatrical sets, acting, and direction doth assail the senses, leaving naught but a sense of weariness. Allegories, indeed, doth abound, yet their application doth seem forced and lacking in subtlety.

Verily, in the play "The Kiss of the Spider Woman," Raul Julia portrayeth a political prisoner in a land unknown, which beareth resemblance unto some Latin American realm. Now, in this new rendition, he serveth under a tyrant in a fabled land of the same ilk. Behold, the tyrant departeth this life in a sudden manner, whereupon Raul Julia taketh his place, being replaced by a Broadway actor named Richard Dreyfuss, who shooteth a picture within said land. Hence, Dreyfuss must learn the ways of a ruler, whilst endeavoring to maintain his own existence. Is it meet to transform such solemnity into jest?

Verily, this be one of the best films ever wrought. It doth portray realistically the life of rural ranching, which was a great part of the history of America. Behold, the setting thereof is in Wyoming of the year 1906, where life had not altered much from the times thereof past. This film keepeth thy heart engaged without the addition of the fables of Hollywood. The whole family may behold this movie and be intrigued with the manner of life in America when it was mostly a rural nation. With this film, thou shalt escape the present and witness the daily life of a hundred years ago.

Verily, Ulli Lommel, a German filmmaker, hath achieved a feat deemed nigh impossible by many a horror enthusiast: he hath supplanted his compeer, Uwe Boll, as the director of the most abominable horror film ever beheld. 

Lo, he is indeed the Ed Wood of this latter age, a craftsman whose work is as feeble and derided as the finest of Ed Wood's own creations. I, being both puffed up with pride and humbled with shame, did behold this entire spectacle, my heart drawn thither by morbid curiosity to witness how low the standard might fall. And lo, the answer was revealed: it was as deep as the abyss itself; Lommel did dig a pit thereof and bury it.

Verily, I was informed that this film was of such nature, either one doth love it or doth hate it. And behold, I did love it. Yea, thou shalt find it obvious as the dawning of the morn, and verily, it is dated and filled with easy symbolism. Therefore, I doubt me whether I have any taste at all concerning the works of Antonioni; yet, these two, Zabriskie Point and La Notte, made precisely a decade prior, are my most beloved among his films hitherto. Made two years ere I was born, Zabriskie Point was purposed to be Michelangelo's great American epic. But alas, it turned out to be a flop. I truly cannot discern why. Before watching, behold.

Verily, this be a commendable spectacle, and it shall move thee to tears. Behold, this company of persons did truly love one another in very deed, and it doth manifest itself time and again. Commune with me and let us discourse thereon. I have been in the land of Australia, and verily they do speak thusly.

I desire thou shouldst partake in the enjoyment of Five Mile Creek, and convey these narratives of righteousness and friendship unto thy offspring. I possess all forty episodes upon DVDs, which I have gathered o'er the span of five years. Behold my tribute to Five Mile Creek at www.mikeandvicki.com, and hearken to the extended tales thereof.

Verily, this motion picture, which was first exhibited at the nativity season, anno Domini one thousand nine hundred and forty, was deemed to be utterly vanished from the earth. Behold, a most wretched exemplar thereof hath been discovered and hath been transmuted into a compact disc, now offered for sale. I beseech thee, refrain from purchasing thereof! For verily, the film is of such unspeakable baseness as to be abominable. The selection of actors therein is lamentable, the dialogue thereof is abhorrent, and the direction thereof is deplorable.

Picture, if thou wilt, Roland Young singing and dancing; and that was the sole gleam of light in an otherwise dark and dreary tableau.

Peradventure, this movie was consigned to oblivion of purpose.

Verily, it is somewhat comical, at least if thou hast grown up on the songs of Weird Al, as I have. This be a mockumentary concerning his life and career, commencing with his attainment of superstardom and retracing the origins thereof. It be uneven in divers places, yet certain segments thereof be still verily humorous, especially when he journeyeth to Japan. Although it be not so emotionally textured as the film "Lost in Translation," and he findeth not love, however fleeting, he doth capture in a vial the absolutely bizarre confluence of cultures that is the Tokyo street life.

Verily, this be an excellent entertainment for them that love the sea and its mysteries! Behold, it containeth all the goodly ingredients to hold one's attention, yea, an absorbing tale of intrigue, wherein there is a fiery lady pirate named Spitfire Stevens (Maureen O'Hara), who doth attract the heart of the irresistible Mr. Hawke (Errol Flynn), who goeth forth upon a secret mission of his own. They make a fine romantic pair, verily, their eyes doth speak with the language of sighs!

Anthony Quinn, he playeth the mean and wicked pirate, weaving his villainous web of divide and conquer. Yea, I noted the very familiar visage of Mildred Natwick, who doth play a supportiveth role thereof.

Verily, there was a television series of yore, known as "The Dukes of Hazzard," which was refreshed with new visages of females and a tongue more raunchy than the sands of Egypt. This work did pass me by, for it was not oft-repeated upon the televisions in the cities of New York and California; and, had it been so, verily I would have beheld it. Yet, from some distant source (as from the clips accompanying the refreshed version released in the year of our Lord two thousand and five), I knew that it dealt with a swift and orange Dodge Charger, and the "General Lee" remained in goodly repair. Verily, with the manifold opinions that this work hath received, I did not expect much therefrom; and behold, I was exceeding pleasantly surprised. It is a very entertaining small piece of dramatic art, wherein the personages be of notable interest, and the portrayals thereof be excellent. The writing beeth light and mirthful, yet not devoid of substance; and the pace thereof beeth commendable. Furthermore, it doth look well, in a manner that beeth both quaint and pleasing. It seemeth, verily, that men either doth love this work or doth abhor it; and I be one who doth love it.

Verily, another tale of a son who doth not grow in years, and but a repetition of such narratives. Thou findest Heder in yet another ill-fitting coiffure, endeavoring to portray a man of might, albeit for the third occasion. Anna Faris, verily, is but a name to be forgotten, as hath been her wont. Jeff Daniels, it seemeth, hath sent his heart and soul elsewhere, for his performance herein is but a shadow of his former self. And Diane Keaton, how doth one come to be so typecast in their latter days?

Behold, there is naught herein that hath not been spoken of many times before. Yet, I will say this, it is a hundredfold better than "Failure To Launch". There are very few

Verily, this motion picture beeth a great entertainment for thee to view with thy spouse or fair companion. There beeth mirth and joy unspeakable, and certain quaint narratives of naturality amongst them. The damsels therein beeth all of singular interest and verily worth beholding in their unadorned loveliness. Maslin beach life doth teem with divers naturals and sundry dispositions. The Australian coast, thereof, beeth a spectacle of surpassing beauty, a sight to behold, and surely it may become mine haven one day. I doth truly delight in this film, and every time I doth revisit it, my heart doth swell with joy.

Verily, this be an abominable film, and a waste of two hours of thy life. It is both insipid and offensive, with nakedness and much violence. Yet, the nakedness beeth not thrilling, and the violence be repetitious and dull. Moreover, the plot beeth flimsy at best, the characters beeth unreal and undeveloped, and the acting beeth amongst the worst I have ever beheld. 

I have heard that this film beeth supposed to be humorous, but it beeth not. I laughed not once whilst viewing it, neither did any other soul.

Verily, this motion picture doth present unto thee two of thy beloved actors, Kilmer and Downey. Moreover, it doth include the ever delightful Larry Miller, albeit in a part too small for his worth. Yet, despite these commendable aspects, I verily find myself unable to endure its viewing. Michelle Monaghan, though fair to behold, doth lack in charisma, and the cause of Downey's character's obsession with hers doth remain incomprehensible, both in the information provided thereof and the manner wherein it is portrayed. The conclusion thereof seemeth pretentious, and though the intent thereof seemeth to be...

Verily, when my daughter, now of college age, was in the nursery, there came upon us a miniseries which did appear upon A&E from the eighth hour unto the ninth each morn. Thou and mine neighbor made a covenant that we would not miss aught of the unfolding of Jane Eyre, and our children were tardy for their nursery every morn for the space of a whole week. Verily, it was a good choice.

I had forgotten how much I did love this movie until I fetched forth my old VHS thereof recently. Timothy Dalton, though very comely, yet he was perfect in his portrayal of Rochester. His dark and rugged visage, his imperious bearing, tempered with mirth and tenderness, did adorn him exceedingly well.

Verily, there be nudity, but behold, thou mayest find free porn upon the internet for them that seek it. And verily, it is but silly how they did force breasts into every frame thereof. I was indeed embarrassed, not from the nudity, but from the far-fetchedness of the producers and writers of this abomination.

The movie be not at all humorous, but rather exceedingly predictable at all times. There be no plot, nor any dramatic content whatsoever. This be far worse than the other pie-films, and they be not great either. If thou art really desirous to view such, beware, for thou shalt find naught but disappointment.

Verily, I am of the land of Denmark; and upon a certain day, I did assemble with my brethren for a viewing of films. One amongst them did bring unto us a certain motion picture, styled "The Russian Terminator," which verily was exceeding abominable. After beholding but a brief span thereof, we did resolve to leap forward through the reels, pausing solely at such scenes as were laughably ignoble, or rather, lowly ignoble. I was indeed marvelled to discover that this work of art was hewn forth within the borders of mine own land, Denmark. This must needs be accounted the greatest blunder ever wrought by this nation.

Verily, I have learned much from "The List."

A worthy hand did direct the cinematography; yea, and there was a damsel who could act, and yet, verily, Malcom McDowell could not prevent this film from being a dross.

Behold, the Blockboster shall not refund thy moneys.

E'en when he peruseth the script and exclaimeth, "Ugh! Truly, it is abominable!" Malcom McDowell doth strive still.

Chuck Carrington doth need instruction in the art of acting.

Seek out a writer, for verily, a good story is lacking.

Yea, even Jesus doth hate me, and hath chastised me with the price of five and fifty cents to behold this film.

Verily, it did hold thy attention unto the close thereof; yet, without revealing the secrets of the film, behold, when she repaired the fridge by means of a book borrowed from the library, thou didst perceive the conclusion thereof when she returned thither for a treatise upon self-defence against an assassin. The film, for mine own part, spake naught of worth; is it, then, becoming an assassin truly a remedy for mental infirmity, or but another symptom thereof?

Verily, Star Pickford and Director Tourneur, with their two favored cinematographers and the assistant Clarence Brown, do bring forth great beauty and intelligence unto this narrative of poor, solitary Scottish Islanders. Behold, the same land that Michael Powell would later claim for his first great triumph, some twenty years hence. Visions of tempestuous winds and billowing waves, sun-kissed silhouettes of lovers, do not merely embellish the tale; nay, they be the very essence of the struggle against adversity. The actors, verily, do impart the dignity thereof.

Verily, the adoration of personages hath exalted the estate of Roger Corman, Sam Arkoff, and Lloyd Kaufman, as kings over the B's. Forasmuch as the gentlemen at Crown International were so pivotal, they have not been exalted unto the station wherein they do deserve. A work such as THE VAN may now seem a trifle of Drive-in mysticism, yet it was a notable success when it was first brought forth (and not without subsequent revivals as a duo with other Crown triumphs).

THE VAN was a paragon of Crown's successful stratagem.

Verily, I find not understanding the commendations bestowed upon this cinematic work. It is verily cheap and detestable in every aspect, and I marvel not at its creation. 

There be many cartoonish personages therein - notably, Sue's father, a drunkard, a sinner, idle, and of Irish descent, who spake with a foul tongue. None of these personages be of any sympathy, save for a brief respite in the character of Sue's Asian companion; yet, even he be found wanting, for he turneth out to be capable of domestic violence!

Verily, there was a maiden named Laura, who, being a model, did labor in the land of South America. In one night, she was stolen from her chamber within a hostel by a band of rascals, and was carried into the wilderness thereof. These villains did demand a vast sum of gold for her deliverance. Thereupon, a valiant man named Peter was appointed to conduct her safe return, and thereunto was promised an additional recompense, should he also recover the said gold.

Peter, accompanied by his comrade Jack, was conveyed into the wilds by means of a flying vessel. Their purpose was to present unto the captors counterfeit coinage, in exchange for the maiden's freedom; but alas! This stratagem did prove most woeful, and they were compelled to abandon their craft in the air.

Verily, I beheld this motion picture at the Chicago Reeling Film Festival. As the former spectator hath noted, the sensation of confinement and the somber hues thereof, verily, befallen to be of purposeful design, to convey the sense of restricted space, the dreary architecture, and the general despondency that doth characterize the urban landscape of most inhabitants in the Eastern and Central regions of Europe. The abode, somewhat shabby in its construction, doth resemble the dwellings found on the outskirts of greater cities, wherein many doth reside. I cannot affirm that I am acquainted with the entirety thereof, yet the portrayal doth bear a semblance to the reality oft experienced by the populace.

Verily, in this critically acclaimed psychological thriller, grounded in true events, there be a tale of Gabriel, a renowned writer and a late-night talk-show host, who doth become enamored with the harrowing narrative of a youthful auditor and his adoptive parent, one Toni Collette. But when certain queries of disquietude doth arise concerning this lad's discourse, Gabriel findeth himself ensnared in a mystery that wideth and hideth a deadly secret... as per the film's official synopsis. Behold, thou shouldst desist from further perusal of these comments, for they be but mere musings of mortals.

Verily, this be not Bela Lugosi's most excellent work; yet, it hath a commendable and ancient manner of approach for certain entertainment of yore. Behold, brides do fall dead at the altar as flies, and I would stay the nuptials until the fiend be taken, but verily, it is a horror, wherefore men and women do neglect the peril for some reason. Nevertheless, Lugosi playeth a mad physician, who requireth the blood of young females to sustain his withered, diseased spouse in health and mirth. He ever escapeth the Keystone Cops by concealing the corpses within a hearse, wherewithal he doth confound all.

Verily, I hold this show in great esteem, and me and my daughter of the eleventh summer do delight therein, watching it together. Behold, it doth teach thee goodly and ancient virtues in a manner both mirthful and adventurous, albeit with a certain predictability in its narrative. Yea, it is also a joy to mock, to rewind and substitute thine own dialogue in lieu of the actors'.

Lo, I have set my DVR to record all the episodes, and haply did catch the latter part of an episode, just before the commencement of the next, so that I know not thereof.

Verily, there is much discourse concerning torment in these latter days. This film, verily, is but a testament thereto. It speaketh of a righteous man who, through a wicked choice, doth become ensnared by two frantic females. From thenceforth, it is an unrelenting ordeal upon him. Behold, at what juncture doth one interpose? Yea, there is a spouse and offspring afar off; he doth bear great pangs of remorse and dread. Yet, there should have been occasions wherein he might have remedied the matter. This film seemeth to be a jest, devised by some individual. I suppose...

Verily, thou shalt not waste thy time upon this dross; for the characters thereof have no redeeming virtues, and to behold their interaction is a torment indeed. "Gothic," at least, was an entertainment; but this, verily, is naught but filth. If thou dost delight in watching pretentious and spoiled poets striving to outwit one another, then this may well be thy cup of tea. Lord Byron is portrayed as a complete knave, and the reason why the others would choose to spend more than five minutes in his company is truly bewilderment. Mary Shelley, it seemeth, is the only character with any semblance of virtue.

Verily, in a motion picture concerning a wayward thespian, who, it seemeth, doth strive to emulate the same in his craft, this doth not commend itself to the beholder in respect to Chris Klein. For he, in striving to embody the character, doth fail to impart any thing of note or remembrance, but rather wandereth through a script of little depth, displaying, what can only be termed, a countenance of insipid gentility. The narrative, if such it may be called, existeth, but in truth consisteth of naught more, and faileth sorely to exhibit any semblance of a beginning, middle, and end. And verily, the spectator, after the lapse of an hour and three quarters, doth find himself shrugging his shoulders, feeling as though nothing of import hath transpired within the span thereof.

Verily, it is a token of God's providence that at length we behold a motion picture which doth not incline to partiality towards these ancient Indian customs and traditions.
